questions.def: 'Although' and 'nevertheless' contrast, creating a complex sentence.
questions.question: Although it was raining, ___ we decided to go for a walk.

questions.def: 'Once' introduces a time clause, combining it with the main clause.
questions.question: ___ the rain stopped, we went outside.

questions.def: 'Despite' does not need 'of'. It directly modifies the noun phrase.
questions.question: Despite of the fact that it was late, they stayed.

questions.def: A perfect participle clause shows the action happened before the main clause.
questions.question: ___ the two companies ___, they became a market leader.

questions.def: 'Even though' introduces a contrast between the clauses.
questions.question: ___ he had studied hard, he failed the exam.

questions.def: 'As' introduces a manner clause specifying how he finished.
questions.question: He finished the report ___ I asked him to.

questions.def: A perfect participle clause gives the reason for the main clause's event.
questions.question: ___ the flight ___, we missed our connection.

questions.def: 'Though' creates a contrasting clause, adding unexpected information.
questions.question: She didn't call, ___ I expected her to.

questions.def: 'Despite' is followed by a gerund, showing contrast.
questions.question: ___ being tired, he continued working.

questions.def: A perfect participle clause shows completed action before the main event.
questions.question: ___ his work ___, he went home.

questions.def: 'Even if' creates a hypothetical contrast, showing a persistent feeling.
questions.question: ___ she apologized, I still felt hurt.

questions.def: 'So that' indicates purpose, the reason for speaking loudly.
questions.question: He spoke loudly ___ everyone could hear him.

questions.def: The perfect passive participle indicates a prior action affecting reaction.
questions.question: ___ of the change, everyone reacted calmly.

questions.def: 'Regardless of' introduces a factor that doesn't change the opinion.
questions.question: ___ the cost, the product is excellent.

questions.def: 'Despite' introduces a contrasting element to the main clause.
questions.question: ___ the fact that he was late, he still got the job.

questions.def: A perfect participle shows completed action before the main verb action.
questions.question: ___ the instructions ___, he completed the task.

questions.def: 'Despite' introduces a contrasting factor to the main point.
questions.question: ___ being expensive, the car is very reliable.

questions.def: 'As' here means 'at the same time', linking the two actions.
questions.question: He left ___ I arrived.

questions.def: A perfect participle clause explains what happened before.
questions.question: ___ his degree ___, he looked for a job.

questions.def: 'Even though' shows a contrast; expected outcome didn't happen.
questions.question: ___ the traffic was bad, we arrived on time.

questions.def: 'When' introduces a time clause, indicating when the action will occur.
questions.question: I will call you ___ I arrive.

questions.def: Passive perfect participle indicates prior action affected current one.
questions.question: ___ about the danger, they proceeded carefully.

questions.def: 'Despite being' introduces a contrast with a gerund phrase.
questions.question: ___ I was tired, I finished the project.

questions.def: 'So that' indicates purpose; the reason for the explanation.
questions.question: He explained the problem ___ I could understand it.

questions.def: Although introduces a contrast; 'nevertheless' strengthens that contrast.
questions.question: Although it was raining, ___ we decided to go for a walk.

questions.def: In 'unless' clauses, use the present simple to refer to the future.
questions.question: Unless it ___ raining soon, the match will be cancelled.

questions.def: 'Due to' requires a noun phrase. 'Because of' is better.
questions.question: Due to the fact that he was ill, he didn't come.

questions.def: 'As reported' introduces a dependent clause acting as an adverbial.
questions.question: ___, the company is doing well.

questions.def: 'In order' shows purpose; it explains WHY she studied hard.
questions.question: She studied hard, ___ to pass the exam.

questions.def: 'As if' introduces a hypothetical situation, requiring the subjunctive.
questions.question: He acted ___ he was the manager.
